title: When Doctors Were Slow to Sign Up, Vezeeta Turned to Patients
conflicts: First funding: Barsoum (Startup Scene, 2018) says TDF put in $1.3 million and the founders about $300,000; Wamda (2014) reports TDF/Ideavelopers took 40% for EGP 8 million (over $1.1 million). Story gives Barsoum's figures as his account plus Wamda's 40% stake. Co-founder spelled Ahmad Bader (Wamda) or Ahmed Badr (Startup Scene, Beco); story uses Ahmed Badr. Outcome figures are all company-supplied and dated (50,000 patients in 2014; 4.5 million users in January 2020), and are attributed.
notes: Slate said founding-decision in 2012; the documented episode is the 2012-13 change of direction from clinic software (DrBridge) to patient booking (Vezeeta, launched September 2013), so arc is change-of-direction and approx_date 2013-09. Healthcare story but talQen not mentioned, per assignment.
